dossier.purpose: MIT-licensed SDK/library monorepo (Python workspace under python/ and .NET solution under dotnet/; the Go SDK is a separate repo, README.md:17) for building agents and graph-based multi-agent workflows. It ships provider chat clients (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Foundry, Anthropic, Bedrock and others), tools, sessions/history, MCP/A2A/AG-UI support, checkpointed workflows, OpenTelemetry, Foundry hosting, and a 'harness' layer (HarnessAgent in .NET, create_harness_agent in Python) that wraps any supplied chat client with planning todos, plan/execute modes, file memory, skills, compaction, tool approval, looping and background sub-agents. It also ships wrappers around external agent SDKs (Claude Agent SDK, Python only; GitHub Copilot SDK, Python and .NET) and separate sandbox/shell packages (Hyperlight, Monty, Docker/local shell, LocalCodeAct). No worker daemon, task queue, or packaged deep-research product exists at this revision: the only console scripts are devui and Lab tools (python/packages/devui/pyproject.toml:44-45; python/packages/lab/pyproject.toml:96-98) and dotnet/src has no executable project.

claims.claim: MAF is an open, multi-language framework for building production-grade AI agents and multi-agent workflows in .NET and Python.

Provides a consistent foundation across Python, .NET and Go; supports Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI and the GitHub Copilot SDK, with samples and hosting patterns for local development and cloud deployment. The Go SDK lives in a separate repository (microsoft/agent-framework-go).

Strong fit if you run agents in production, need orchestration beyond a stateless chat loop, want sequential/concurrent/handoff/group patterns, care about durability, restartability, observability, governance or human-in-the-loop control, and need provider flexibility.
Python and C#/.NET Support: 'Full framework support for both Python and C#/.NET implementations with consistent APIs'.
Orchestration Patterns & Workflows: graph-based workflows (sequential, concurrent, handoff, group collaboration) that 'include checkpointing, streaming, human-in-the-loop, and time-travel'.
Foundry Hosted Agents (new): deploy and host agents to Foundry-hosted infrastructure 'with just 2 additional lines of code'.
Observability: built-in OpenTelemetry integration for distributed tracing, monitoring and debugging.
AF Labs: experimental packages for benchmarking, reinforcement learning and research initiatives; installed separately via agent-framework-lab.
pip install agent-framework installs the standard package set (experimental Lab modules are separate).
Durable Task and Azure Functions samples live in a separate Durable Agent Framework extension repository, not in this repo.
Using third-party servers, agents, code or non-Azure-direct models is at the user's own risk; users must review data flows and implement their own responsible-AI mitigations.

create_harness_agent builds a pre-configured, batteries-included agent: function invocation, per-service-call persistence, compaction, TodoProvider, AgentModeProvider (plan/execute), memory/skills/shell (when provided), tool approval, looping and OpenTelemetry; each feature can be disabled or customized.

.NET HarnessAgent is an opinionated pre-configured agent 'suitable for interactive agentic scenarios such as research, coding, data analysis, and general task automation', assembled around a caller-supplied IChatClient with function invocation, per-service-call history persistence, optional compaction, context providers and decorators.

LocalShellTool 'is not a sandbox' (the boundary is approval-in-the-loop). Sandbox tiers: Hyperlight WASM microVM for untrusted code, DockerShellTool OCI container for untrusted shell, LocalShellTool approval-in-the-loop for trusted dev.

readme.telemetry_and_network: Besides the items below, no other phone-home was found in the telemetry, client-setup and hosting paths reviewed. (1) HTTP header stamping, on by default: the Python OpenAI client merges 'agent-framework-version: python/<ver>' and a 'agent-framework-python/<ver>' User-Agent prefix into its default headers (python/packages/openai/agent_framework_openai/_shared.py:197-201); disable with env AGENT_FRAMEWORK_USER_AGENT_DISABLED=true|1 (python/packages/core/agent_framework/_telemetry.py:19-30,210-211). A coarse boolean feature-usage mask '(feat=vN.hex)' is appended to User-Agent only for approved HTTPS Azure/Foundry origins (cognitiveservices.azure.com, openai.azure.com, services.ai.azure.com; python/packages/openai/agent_framework_openai/_feature_usage.py:24-28,61-67) and is disabled by AGENT_FRAMEWORK_FEATURE_MASK_DISABLED (python/packages/core/agent_framework/_telemetry.py:21,135-137); design record says no identifiers, prompts, payloads or model names are encoded (docs/decisions/0033-feature-usage-bitmask-user-agent.md:25-48,57-72). .NET: 'agent-framework-dotnet/<version>' User-Agent added on approved Azure origins for the OpenAI client (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI/UserAgentPolicies.cs:9-16; dotnet/src/Shared/FeatureUsage/AgentFrameworkUserAgentPolicy.cs:47-89) and on all Foundry-client requests (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry/AgentFrameworkUserAgentPolicy.cs:9-15); the .NET feature token is disabled by AGENT_FRAMEWORK_FEATURE_MASK_DISABLED=true|1 (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.Abstractions/FeatureUsage.cs:23,40-42,178-183). (2) OpenTelemetry: harness agents wrap OpenTelemetry by default (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.Harness/HarnessAgent.cs:58,190-193; python/packages/core/agent_framework/_harness/_agent.py:699-700); Python instrumentation defaults to enabled but core depends only on opentelemetry-api (python/packages/core/pyproject.toml:30), exporters are developer-configured via OTLP env vars (python/packages/core/agent_framework/observability.py:691-703); sensitive-data capture defaults to False (observability.py:1013-1016; .NET EnableSensitiveData, dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI/OpenTelemetryAgent.cs:28,154); harness README says default telemetry is metadata only (python/samples/02-agents/harness/README.md:169-171). Foundry-hosted runs inject APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING and an OTLP pipeline (dotnet/samples/02-agents/Harness/BuildYourOwnClaw/Claw_Step04_ProductionReady/ClawAgent.Hosted/README.md:24-36). (3) Required services/accounts: a model endpoint - OpenAI API key (python/packages/openai/README.md:49-57), Azure OpenAI/Foundry endpoint plus Azure credential via az login (README.md:111-135,191-198), Anthropic API key (python/samples/02-agents/providers/anthropic/README.md:27-48), or a GitHub Copilot CLI session. Foundry Hosted Agents, the Foundry Deep Research tool (needs a Bing grounding connection and an o3-deep-research deployment, dotnet/samples/02-agents/Agents/Agent_Step15_DeepResearch/README.md:12-18) and FoundryEvals need Azure resources. (4) Build/run-time downloads: the .NET GitHub.Copilot package downloads the Copilot CLI binary at build time unless CopilotSkipCliDownload=true (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot/buildTransitive/Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot.targets:14-25). (5) Local state defaults: harness file memory under {cwd}/agent-file-memory (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.Harness/HarnessAgent.cs:337-347; python/packages/core/agent_framework/_harness/_agent.py:185-190); Foundry-hosting stores as JSON under ~/.agentserver/state_stores outside Foundry (python/packages/foundry_hosting/README.md:93-98); Copilot CLI state under ~/.copilot (python/packages/github_copilot/agent_framework_github_copilot/_agent.py:453-456).

code.architecture: Monorepo with two parallel implementations. Python workspace (python/packages, 41 packages built with flit-core; Lab excluded from the workspace, python/pyproject.toml:71-73). `core` (agent_framework): _agents.py (Agent), _clients.py, _tools.py (function-invocation loop: max_iterations default 40, max_function_calls/max_duration_seconds default None, :104,1851-1856; tool approval_mode default never_require, :667), _sessions.py (sessions, history providers, SessionStore), _compaction.py, _middleware.py, _mcp.py, _skills.py, _workflows/ (graph workflows, _checkpoint.py with InMemory/File storage), _evaluation.py (LocalEvaluator, evaluate_agent, evaluate_workflow), observability.py, security.py, and _harness/ (_agent.py factory, _todo.py, _mode.py, _file_memory.py, _file_access.py, _background_agents.py, _loop.py, _tool_approval.py, _memory.py). Other packages: provider clients (openai, anthropic, foundry, bedrock, gemini, ollama, mistral...), SDK wrappers (claude, github_copilot), sandboxes/tools (hyperlight, monty, tools), hosting (foundry_hosting, hosting, hosting-responses, hosting-a2a, hosting-mcp, hosting-telegram, a2a, ag-ui, devui), stores (azure-cosmos, redis, postgres, ...), orchestrations (sequential/concurrent/handoff/group chat/Magentic) and lab (gaia, tau2, lightning). .NET (dotnet/src, 35 projects): Microsoft.Agents.AI.Abstractions (AIAgent, AgentSession, ChatHistoryProvider, AIContextProvider, FeatureUsage), Microsoft.Agents.AI (ChatClientAgent, decorators, compaction, Harness/ providers: Todo, AgentMode, FileMemory, FileAccess, BackgroundAgents, ToolApproval, Loop), Microsoft.Agents.AI.Harness (HarnessAgent pipeline assembly), Workflows (+Declarative, Generators), provider packages (OpenAI, Anthropic, Foundry, GitHub.Copilot), sandboxes (Hyperlight, LocalCodeAct, Tools.Shell), hosting (Hosting*, Foundry.Hosting), stores (CosmosNoSql, Hosting.AzureStorage, Valkey), Mcp, AgentHooks. Harness pipeline in both languages (HarnessAgent.cs:167-300; _agent.py:659-703): supplied chat client -> function invocation (bounded iterations) -> message injection -> per-service-call history persistence -> optional compaction (only when context/output token budgets are given) -> default context providers (todo, mode, file memory, skills; opt-in file access, background agents, shell) -> tool-approval layer -> optional loop (default max 10 iterations) -> OpenTelemetry; a hosted web-search tool is added when the client supports it (HarnessAgent.cs:312-319; _agent.py:634-644). The harness runs in the host process and contains no model-specific code; isolation comes only from add-ons (Hyperlight, Docker shell, provider-hosted containers, Foundry hosted containers).

claim_checks.evidence: No 'GPT-6.1' or 'Sol' model reference exists in the repo. The only 'gpt-6-sol' string is the stubbed Bedrock Converse model id 'us.openai.gpt-6-sol' in unit tests (python/packages/bedrock/tests/test_bedrock_client.py:125-129,147,504-508). OpenAI, Foundry and Bedrock clients take the model as a free-form string (python/packages/openai/README.md:65-67; python/packages/openai/agent_framework_openai/_chat_client.py:578; python/packages/bedrock/agent_framework_bedrock/_chat_client.py:110,187) and the harness has no model-specific code (HarnessAgent.cs:80-134; _agent.py:312-356). Samples default to gpt-5.4 (dotnet/samples/02-agents/Harness/Harness_Step01_Research/Program.cs:29) and gpt-5.6-luna (python/samples/02-agents/providers/openai/client_prompt_caching.py:71); all harness samples use Foundry clients (Program.cs:72-82; python/samples/02-agents/harness/harness_research.py:99). The GitHub Copilot SDK agent accepts a model string and a BYOK provider config (python/packages/github_copilot/agent_framework_github_copilot/_agent.py:492-518), but nothing in the repo shows a GPT-6.x model reached through it.

risks: No evidence for the stated model or harness pairing: the only 'gpt-6-sol' string is a stubbed Bedrock model id in unit tests (python/packages/bedrock/tests/test_bedrock_client.py:125-129,504-508). The harness is a thin wrapper over whatever chat client is passed (HarnessAgent.cs:80-134), all harness samples use Foundry-hosted Responses clients (Harness_Step01_Research/Program.cs:72-82), and HarnessAgent tests use mocks with no live-model integration test (dotnet/tests/Microsoft.Agents.AI.Harness.UnitTests/HarnessAgentTests.cs:59-100).

Not an isolated, resumable worker runtime by itself: no worker daemon or CLI ships (python/packages/devui/pyproject.toml:44-45; python/packages/lab/pyproject.toml:96-98). Default history is in-memory (HarnessAgent.cs:69-73), in-flight background-agent tasks become Lost after a restart (BackgroundAgentRuntimeState.cs:14-17), crash recovery is Foundry-hosting-only, opt-in, and workflow-only in Python (python/packages/foundry_hosting/agent_framework_foundry_hosting/_responses.py:444-449; dotnet FoundryResponsesOptions.cs:60-84), and Durable Task/Azure Functions hosting lives in another repo (README.md:171,180).

Sandbox tiers are platform-limited and pre-GA: Hyperlight (Python beta, .NET preview) needs /dev/kvm or MSHV/WHP; its Python Wasm backend exists only for linux x86_64 and win32 AMD64 on Python <3.15 and uv environments omit macOS (python/packages/hyperlight/pyproject.toml:28,32-37; python/samples/04-hosting/container/hyperlight_codeact/README.md:45-63); the default Foundry hosted runtime exposes no hypervisor (same README:11-20). LocalCodeAct and LocalShellTool are explicitly not sandboxes (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.LocalCodeAct/README.md:5-8; python/packages/tools/README.md:45-48). Neither CI matrix includes macOS (python-tests.yml:26; dotnet-build-and-test.yml:105-108,184-185).

Fast-moving, partly experimental API surface: Python harness features (background agents, file access, looping, memory, todo storage) are experimental and emit warnings (python/PACKAGE_STATUS.md:126-129; _harness/_agent.py:377-383,572-582); claude, hyperlight, tools, monty, devui and foundry-hosting are beta and the hosting* helpers are alpha (PACKAGE_STATUS.md:20-58); .NET HarnessAgentOptions carries many [Experimental(MAAI001)] members (HarnessAgentOptions.cs:45,62,82,94,165,175,252,264,274,369,379); Python minor releases carry [BREAKING] entries (python/CHANGELOG.md:10,23-26,61,76-81); .NET Anthropic integration tests are disabled in CI (dotnet-build-and-test.yml:460-464).

Bounded tool access is opt-in, not default: Python tools default to approval_mode never_require (python/packages/core/agent_framework/_tools.py:667) and max_function_calls/max_duration_seconds default to None (_tools.py:1851-1856); the .NET harness auto-loads skills (which may carry scripts) from the current directory (HarnessAgent.cs:354-361; python/samples/02-agents/harness/README.md:152-154); ClaudeAgent exposes permission_mode bypassPermissions (python/packages/claude/agent_framework_claude/_agent.py:162,207); FileSystemAgentFileStore is 'not a sandbox against a hostile process' (python/packages/core/agent_framework/_harness/_file_access.py:1217-1219); background agents, external skill sources, loop judges and summarizers extend the trust boundary (python/samples/02-agents/harness/README.md:142-171).

Python workflow checkpoints embed pickle data; the restricted unpickler is 'not a security boundary' and checkpoint storage must be access-controlled and trusted (python/packages/core/agent_framework/_workflows/_checkpoint_encoding.py:18-46). Hosted default stores changed to a scoped v2 namespace without migrating old sessions, checkpoints or approvals, and saved sessions expire 30 days after last write (python/packages/foundry_hosting/README.md:149-158,187-192).

No packaged deep-research harness at this revision. The nearest items are samples: a .NET sample using the Foundry Agent Service Deep Research tool (o3-deep-research plus a Bing grounding connection) through [Obsolete] Persistent Agents APIs (dotnet/samples/02-agents/Agents/Agent_Step15_DeepResearch/Program.cs:3,12-14,27-37; PersistentAgentsClientExtensions.cs:22); a Magentic-style declarative workflow whose search tools are absent or commented out (dotnet/samples/03-workflows/Declarative/DeepResearch/Program.cs:116-121,254-260; python/samples/03-workflows/declarative/deep_research/main.py:162-172); and a harness research assistant that only instructs the model to cite sources inline (python/samples/02-agents/harness/harness_research.py:81-90). Citations exist only as provider-returned annotations (python/packages/core/agent_framework/_types.py:401-412). Evaluation APIs (LocalEvaluator, evaluate_agent, FoundryEvals) are experimental (python/PACKAGE_STATUS.md:92-97).

Support and provenance gaps: Microsoft support covers only Azure-service usage, otherwise GitHub issues (SUPPORT.md:11). Release workflows have no signing, attestation or checksum step and the .NET publish path is not in the repo (.github/workflows/python-release.yml:119-131; dotnet-build-and-test.yml:137-171). Third-party binaries and pins vary: the .NET GitHub.Copilot package downloads a CLI binary at build time (dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot/buildTransitive/Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot.targets:14-25); claude-agent-sdk is a pre-1.0 range (python/packages/claude/pyproject.toml:27); github-copilot-sdk is pinned ==1.0.11 in Python vs 1.0.14 in .NET (python/packages/github_copilot/pyproject.toml:26; dotnet/Directory.Packages.props:115); Hyperlight is 0.7.x in Python vs 0.6.0 in .NET (python/packages/hyperlight/pyproject.toml:26-29; dotnet/Directory.Packages.props:129-130).
